answer: Proof-of-Idle bridge epochs. Each new identity must complete a randomly scheduled idle window before its first transaction, verified by a lightweight beacon emitted only after the window elapses. Traffic arriving faster than the epoch schedule is held at the bridge until real time passes. An attacker mass-registering identities must pay wall-clock latency per identity—a glacier of stalled throughput—so fabricating N sybils costs N sequential waiting periods, not one burst.
